This appeal having been heard and reserved for orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, this court passed the following :
ORDER 1.

This appeal by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 31.08.2013 passed by the Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pipariya,
District Narsinghpur in Claim Case No. 98/2012 on account of inadequacy of amount of compensation and seeking enhancement of the same.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pipariya,
District Narsinghpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute.
Therefore, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.
3. As per the finding of the Tribunal in the case of death of Jayant Kumar, an amount of compensation has been allowed.
The income of deceased was assessed at Rs. 4,700/- per month and total amount of compensation has been awarded is Rs. 6,44,500/- along with interest.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that compensation awarded by the Tribunal by accepting the earning of deceased at Rs.4,700/- is inadequate, looking to the fact that he was a skilled labourer.
He further submitted that Tribunal committed error in not adding the amount towards future prospects and consortium.
So, he submitted that by adding future prospect and on applying adequate multiplier, reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
5. None is present on behalf of the insurance company.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for the appellants and on perusing the record, it is the considered opinion of this Court that Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of deceased at Rs.
4,700/-.
So, there is no need to interfere in this regard.
7. After perusing the record, it is found that Tribunal has not added any amount towards future prospect.

In case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and ors. (2017) Vol. 16 SCC 680, it has been held that if the deceased was self employed on a fixed salary an addition of 40 percent of the established income should be warranted.
